「有时候，许多伟大艺术都发生在我们的脑子里，老实说，我就喜欢这样。我们不必完全理解它才能喜欢它，对吧？哪怕那些字其实是在骂人……嗯，我更偏爱留一点给观者自行解读的艺术，汪。」 ]
rows.raw: " "Hmm, that's a bit of a prickly question, woof. A dealer like me can't get too attached to her stock, or else I'd never sell anything! I wouldn't pick it up if I didn't think it wasn't GREAT ART — yes, I know that everyone has their own tastes, but I still need to sell the art! "It's like… how am I going to talk something up with feeling if I don't believe what I'm saying, woof?" That's a lot of words to dance around your question by answering it without actually answering it. Yeah sure, she likes her entire stock… but what does she enjoy? [rand |"Well, I obviously like glassware a lot, otherwise I wouldn't spend as much time as I do in Tychris, woof!" You've seen what the palace has to offer, especially in the chapel of Nareva. It's impressive, to say the least. "It's not just art, it's a way of life in the principality, woof! Even the humblest of people have glassware heirlooms that've been passed down from before the Godswar — stained and colored glass, mirrors, mugs… the 'manders have made it a point of pride for themselves. "They've got all kinds of glass down in the lower city, woof. Whether it's something that catches the light just so, or reinforced glass that can take a hammer blow without cracking — they mix some kind of powdered alloy into the glass before it sets — you can find glass for just about anything. It's famous all the way down into the heartlands, woof!" Which is fair enough.[pc.swornGod nareva | Since you're Nareva's champion and all, getting acquainted with Tychris as a whole once this entire business calms down wouldn't be a bad idea. ] |"Well… I'm carrying some Valgardian fertility charms at the moment! They're traditionally carved by the goblin and kobold tribes as gifts for friends, woof!" She points over at some rather curvaceous figurines on display. "I know that dealing in them does diminish the meaning somewhat, since they're supposed to be gifted by the one who carved them, but I just like them so much I couldn't help but want to pass them on, woof!" Huh. Examining the carved wooden figurines, you can guess why Electra's so into them: each and every one is just as [kohaku.wellFed |ridiculously hourglass-shaped as she is. Not that the little dog[silly|go]'s waist is by any means narrow for her height, it's just that what's above and below is so generous that it's an hourglass anyway, proportionally speaking. Mostly goblin make, then. |pear-shaped as she is. A sympathetic affinity, to be certain — the resemblance is so close as to be uncanny, one can't help but wonder if these were carved just for Electra. But Valgarde is so far away, and on a different continent to boot, isn't it? Well. Your guess is that these are of mostly kobold make, then. ] "Yep! It's good to have friends everywhere, woof!" |"Well, I like these candied gourds." Electra points to a tightly wrapped package of greased paper on her stall. "Really good stuff, never spoils; would have to in order to come all the way across the world here to Tychris!" Oh, really? If these snacks come all the way from afar… where did they come from, then? "Macah, near the border with that two-tailed catfolk peninsula — they really put a lot of work into their sweetmeats, woof! Everything's supposed to be a tonic of some sort and good for you, they're really big on their medicines in that country! "Don't be fooled — it's not really medicinal, or at least not very much so. But it's a nice excuse to have a treat, and it certainly looks and smells that way, woof!" Hmm. Out of curiosity, you pick up the package; even through the wrapping and at arm's length, a sweet scent tinged with pungent herbs meets your nose. It's… well, whether it's great is debatable, but it's definitely an attempt at art of the olfactory kind. Not to everyone's tastes, but isn't that how art is? "I have to try very hard not to eat the goods, woof. Such a constant temptation," Electra sighs. "But it's testament to the fact that GREAT ART should engage all the senses, not just sight. That kind of art doesn't, can't belong in a museum, but for the someone who has the fortune to appreciate it while it lasts, it's absolutely an explosion, woof!" |"I did pick up some of the usual while I was in town, woof," Electra says, reaching into her gigantic pack and pulling out several leather-bound volumes. "Real goatskin, too, for that authentic classical Belharan feel!" [pc.bg acolyte scholar |Hey… you recognize some of those from your scholarship — or at least, the titles on the spines. Quasi-religious texts of Nareva, snippets of folklore, proverbs and sayings attributed to the goddess all rolled into a single volume. They were kind of popular for a while in your small slice of academia such as it was, and never really completely fell out of favor. "Oh yes, woof!" Electra gleefully rubs her hands and wags her ail even harder. "You understand what I'm getting at — my best customers for Nareva's written wisdom are all well-educated people!" Makes sense — that'd be the kind of person most inclined to sing praises for the goddess of magic and secrets. But now that Electra mentions it, while many of your peers happened to possess copies of such proverbs and sayings, you never actually saw anyone reading them… |They look very impressive, but… does she mind if you take a look, have a feel? "You damage it, you bought it, woof!" Fair enough. You receive one of the heavy volumes from Electra, crack it open to the scent of new ink and binding glue — and are immediately faced with lines upon lines of tiny words printed on the pages. There's nothing wrong with it — everything's legible enough and it is what it claims to be, just that it's all very intimidating. Yes, one wouldn't expect anything less from a snippet — relatively speaking — from the goddess of magic and secrets, but this is as unfriendly to any potential reader as writing can ever possibly get. Does anyone actually read this? "Of course not, woof, even if they're actual books good and proper." Wait, what? You weren't being completely serious, but — ] "Well, of course, woof. They're awfully dry — I tried working my way through one of the volumes while on a long carriage trip and fell asleep before I'd even finished a third, woof." … "People don't buy these collections to read Nareva's proverbs, woof. They buy them to be GREAT ART, and that means putting them prominently on shelves with all their attention-catching spines so that people will notice and admire them. Then they have deep and meaningful conversations about everything regarding the books, save for what's actually written in them." [pc.bg acolyte scholar |That's… more or less what your scholarly peers did. |That's about what you expected. Disappointing, but what you expected. ] "I'm just an art dealer. If people will pay me for GREAT ART, then it's what I carry, woof. And I get paid very well for these large black books, which is why I always pick up a couple while in Tychris." |"I do have some fine hanging scrolls from across the ocean, woof!" Grinning, Electra picks up a particular piece from her stall and presents it to you proudly, unrolling it so you can see the ink and brushwork. [kohaku.met |You'd know this particular style pretty well, having seen it all over the kitsune den. ]"These are really hard to get one's hands on, and they just ooze refinement, don't they?" Electra goes through a couple of these — a picture of a dog, the ocean, and a bunch of flowers. The aesthetic is as foreign as it gets, and you note that each scroll comes with couplets to either side of the illustration that very decidedly aren't in Belharan. Do they actually mean anything? "Wouldn't know, woof. I can't read those particular languages — these certainly didn't come to me first-hand. Picked them up from travelers like you." And people hang them up without knowing what the writing means? "Oh yes! So long as they look good, not many people actually care — most people assume it's just the artist signing the piece or something." Electra grins. "The point of these artworks is to look foreign and make the owner appear a little less parochial, woof. So long as that's a given, who cares about what the characters actually mean? As long as it's not a curse or anything, it'll pass — it's not like anyone who actually understands the language will be coming along anytime soon, right? "Sometimes, a lot of GREAT ART happens in our heads, and honestly, I like it that way. We don't have to understand everything about it to like it, right? And even if the writing is just some kind of insult… well, I prefer art that leaves a little to the viewer's interpretation, woof." ] "

rows.original: [flags.ELECTRA_FUCKED|"A repeat customer, woof?" Little Electra's so excited, the golden doggo can't help but bounce in place; it doesn't escape your notice that the motion's deviously calculated to make the little art merchant's [kohaku.wellFed|tits and ]thighs tremble and jiggle against her robes. An innocent coincidence, no doubt. "Ah, no doubt my selection of GREAT ART has such charm, that even the Savior of Tychris can't help but keep coming back for more?" Something along those lines. Whatever else, [kohaku.wellFed |Electra does have the kind of body one usually finds on ancient Valgardian fertility idols. "Lots of those being carved these days, woof. Not exactly ancient, but definitely fertile." Grinning up at you, Electra pinches her hips and tummy, tail wagging. "Maybe some of those rubbed off on me while I was dealing in them; I just can't lose this extra weight no matter how much I hike around doing business, woof." Hey, it's enough to make her look motherly and well-cared for, without being saggy. You'd call that a win when it comes to aesthetic appeal, it's a form that's recognized the world over. |Electra does have a certain kind of appeal for those who prefer the petite. "Well, I'm no stick. Walking everywhere has its benefits." Grinning up at you, Electra pinches her hips and tummy, tail wagging. "I don't mind, it gives my backpack somewhere comfortable to rest on while I'm getting around, woof." Really now, when you know from experience how sensitive it is? Ah well, it's what they say about art, that it opens a window into the mind of the artist. Understand the creator by studying the creation. ] "And that's why you're such a great customer, woof!" Electra's tail wags so fast it's a bushy blur. "Peddling art is one thing, but giving a piece a home with someone who knows how to appreciate it… well, that's something else altogether, woof!" Well. This particular piece is only rented out, but you share her sentiments. If she doesn't mind holding a private viewing, then? Electra beams. "Give me a little bit to wrap up everything, and I'll be right with you, woof!" The little dog[silly|go] is good to her word, closing several last sales before collapsing her stall and stowing it in her backpack — one swears that it has to be bigger on the inside in order to hold everything that she puts in it. Hefting it on her shoulders, she takes your hand and starts tugging excitedly, pointing at the palace. No further payments? What a deal you're getting here. [kohaku.anyKids |A weak smile. "Like I said before, you've already paid, woof. And given the price the both of us came up with, it'll last a lifetime. Depending on how things go, there may be more purchases, but this will do for now, woof." A sudden heavy silence hangs in the air for a second, then Electra brightens as if nothing had passed between you. "So! Shall we be off, woof?" |"Oh, I almost forgot! Well, if you want to pay some more, I won't stop you, woof!" Gladly. You reach [pc.heightRange 58 66|up|down|over] and firmly plant your fingers atop Electra's head, letting your fingers sink into her thick, fluffy hair. Through the outer guard hairs, down into the poofy stuff below, and finally right to her scalp, you give the little dog[silly|go] as firm a patting as you can manage, ruffling her thick hair. Slowly, Electra's eyes glaze over, her tail wags all the more furiously, and she starts panting as her cheeks color; the entire petting leaves the little golden dog[silly|go] breathless and dizzy, pulling on you as her knees buckle and threaten to give way altogether. "Consider myself sold, woof," Electra mumbles, shaking out her mussed hair and fur to a smatter of applause from her patrons. "Let's be off, [pc.name]." ] Without further ado, you lead Electra to the palace, where you [party.hasCompanions |let [party.compNames] off for a while before heading to ]find a spare guest room. "I heard you right, didn't I, woof? You wanted to buy something from me?" If she wants to put it in a way she can easily wrap her mind around… then yes. Be that as it may…" Electra shoves her tiny hand into yours. "The price has already been paid, woof, and the goods are yours to deal with as you see fit." She really cost that much, did she? "More than you may ever know, woof." [pc.cunningRange 65 |Somehow, you think you do, and it was worth it; you have no regrets. |Well, if you didn't notice it being paid, it can't have been that steep a price, can it? ] A weak smile. "You have no idea, woof." Be that as it may, it's not going to stop you from savoring the goods. Shall you be off, then, to appreciate some — ahem — great art? |Electra grins, her jovial doggy nature perking up along with her bushy tail. "I heard you right, didn't I, woof? Normally, I'd wouldn't even put it up for sale, but you're special, woof. And before you ask, you're not getting a discount — your specialness means the deal's open to you to begin with!" And what's her price? The little dog[silly|go] merchant leans over her stall. "Are you sure, woof? I don't come cheap, especially during business hours when I could be dealing in the GREAT ART of Tychris. Accommodation in the palace district is also pretty expensive, which is why I usually don't bother with it — but I'd have to insist if that's what you wish of me, woof." Which is fair; a golden work of art deserves nothing less than the finest surroundings to be admired in. Now then, it's time for her to state this price of hers, the one she's so sure you can't pay. "A pat on the head, woof!" Tch. As expected, she drives a hard bargain, but you have to admit — if grudgingly — that's she's worth it. Reaching [pc.heightRange 58 66|up|down|over], you firmly plant your fingers atop Electra's head, letting your fingers sink into her thick, fluffy hair. Through the outer guard hairs, down into the poofy stuff below, and finally right to her scalp, you give the little dog[silly|go] as firm a patting as you can manage, ruffling her thick hair. Slowly, Electra's eyes glaze over, her tail wags all the more furiously, and she starts panting as her cheeks color. The little show hasn't escaped the notice of her clientele, who start chuckling and and shaking their heads as Electra leans into you with a moan. Glad you're putting a show on for them, but the important thing right now is this fine piece of merchandise you've just bought. There, is that good enough? "Truly… a work of art." Electra heaves a deep breath, but clarity of mind continues to evade her and she eventually settles for being even more of a happy dog[silly|go] than usual. The whole melodrama earns you a smattering of applause from the crowd as Electra finally finds her footing, smiling woozily. "Well! The galleries in this part of town aren't open to the likes of us, woof!. But there's a nice place overlooking the plaza that lets out pretty nice rooms, I sometimes stay there at the end of the day —" You'll do her one better. Since you're allowed into the palace, a piece of great art like her surely deserves the best backdrop to be laid against; you're sure that there's a guest chamber or two you can occupy for a bit. After all, being the savior of Tychris has to come with some benefits, doesn't it? "T-the palace? I, well, um —" She's not uneasy about having an entire army of gothmanders buzzing around under her feet, is she? "O-of course not! It's just that the palace, it —" Electra deflates. "It's a lot to take in, woof. Well, let me wrap up for the day…" Electra's little stall is easily put away in her backpack, and with her in hand you make across the plaza for the palace. Gaining entry isn't hard — neither you nor Electra are strangers to the sentries — and finding an empty room [party.hasCompanions |plus entertainment for [party.compNames] ] until evening isn't difficult, either. [kohaku.anyKids |Electra seems extra protective of her backpack every step through the palace — normally, it wouldn't be anything off given the nature of the knick-knacks she peddles vis-a-vis the gothmanders being in so close proximity, but oddly enough she appears to be more concerned about something inside Oh well. ] But eventually, the two of you are alone, and Electra's backpack outside — the furniture in the guest chamber is all 'mander-sized, which only highlights how petite the little golden doggo is and how [kohaku.wellFed |much of a shortstack |bottom-heavy ] she is under that dress of hers. The tension in the air only grows as Electra's bushy tail wags furiously, making her excitement clear; [kohaku.anyKids |to your mild surprise, she makes the first move, eagerly stepping forward and forcing herself into your grasp with a familiarity that would be awkward coming from anyone else, but not from a creature with such a friendly nature |still, you have to beckon her forward before she summons the courage to accept your embrace ]. The little dog[silly|go] [kohaku.wellFed |is as squishy as her curves look |is as slappable below the waist as she looks ], and as firm as a traveling merchant should be underneath; she squeaks and barks as you squeeze her little warm body and feel the fuzziness seep through the fabric of her clothes. Right here in your arms is the essence of small, friendly dog, and one has to admit[pc.isDK|, however begrudgingly]: this is great art indeed. "No buyer's remorse, woof?" Come now, you've barely started. Electra's petite body shivers in your embrace, and you feel her nipples stiffening through her dress as you toy with her floppy dog ears; you're not sure if this is the so-called right way to do it, but you're clearly getting across to her eager canine brain. Sitting down on the bed to steady the both of you, you pull Electra in for a kiss, tongues tussling as your breaths mingle and wash over your cheeks. Her greedy little fingers reach for your [pc.armor], clearly familiar with the style in which it's made and exactly where to pull and tug in order to disrobe you — a little startling, perhaps, but not exactly surprising for someone supposedly as well-travelled as she is. You're supposed to be the one appreciating art here, so you reciprocate her efforts — Electra barks and giggles at your attempts to make sense of her vaguely Tychrisan robe-dress-thing and guides your hands, helping you disrobe her until both your things lie at the foot of the bed in a crumpled mess. "Don't worry about it, woof. This style's long since gone out of fashion in Tychris, [pc.swornGod nareva |I guess you might see it around the order when they get up to dressing all fancy |which is exactly why I picked it to peddle art in ]. But speaking of art… don't you think it's time for an appraisal, woof?" rows.original: [party.som |A |Leaving [companion.name] where [companion.heShe] is and a |Leaving [party.compNames] to occupy themselves and a ]pproaching the librarian’s desk, you are met with an unusual sight: a harpy. It's certainly a little odd to see one of Sorra's chosen in Nareva's seat of power, and the strangeness doesn't end there, either; for starters, she's fully clothed, and quite modestly at that. A soft, woolen sweater and long skirt show off considerably less skin than the garb of any harpy you've seen, and rather than the bright and fiery colors of the harpies out west, her plumage is a gentle brown. Noticing your presence, she [dayNight |looks up at you through a pair of thick, horn-rimmed glasses, her golden, half-lidded eyes conveying a sense of palpable drowsiness |looks up from the tome she had been studying intently, craning her neck at a steep angle ] as she greets you. "[pc.swornGod nareva |Ah! You must be [pc.name]. I was wondering if I might run into you." Without waiting for a response, the stout harpy rises from her chair and extends a clawed hand, which you take. As she gives a polite handshake, the librarian gives you a warm grin, before releasing your hand. You're sorry, but how does she know you? You can't recall ever meeting this woman before. Seeing your confusion, she awkwardly stammers for a few seconds, before composing herself. Clearing her throat, she takes a step back. "A-ah, my apologies! We haven't met in person before, but, well... just about everyone in this cathedral knows of you, [pc.name]. There hasn't been a time in living memory when someone was outright inducted into the Order Astrida, rather than born into it; such news spreads quickly." You suppose that would make sense; given the unusual circumstances, you can hardly be surprised that word got around. Nodding softly, you gesture for her to continue. "A-anyways, allow me to introduce myself. I am Lystra, temporary head of the cathedral's archives. It's my pleasure to finally meet you, [pc.name]." [pc.isDK |Yeah, whatever. You suppose you had to get around to meeting the other people who work here eventually |The pleasure is mutual; getting to know the temple's staff is always a delight ]. With that, Lystra returns to her seat behind the librarian's desk, golden eyes regarding you fondly. "Now then, with introductions out of the way, welcome to the Cathedral of Nareva! As I'm sure you're no doubt aware, you're more than welcome to any of the freely-accessible volumes available here; should you need anything... else, I'm afraid that's a tad outside my wheelhouse. I don't believe we've met before, I seldom forget a face. Regardless, I'd like to welcome you to the Cathedral of Nareva. My name is Lystra, and I am the temporary head of the cathedral's archives. If I may, you are... ]?" You're [pc.name], [a] [pc.title]. [var0 |Recognition flashes over the librarian's face, as she straightens a bit in her seat. [kythie.isMarried |Why, you're the one who married Princess Kythie, aren't you? |You were the one who sorted out... why, yes, I do know you! ]" Rising from her chair, the harpy extends a clawed hand in a gesture of appreciation. rows.original:
As you make your way to Lystra's desk, her eyes light up. Rising from her chair, she meets you as you approach, [lystra.fucked
        |throwing her arms around you in a warm hug
        |extending a hand to shake yours
    ] while you stand confused. What's all this about?
    
    Lystra steps back, excitement gleaming in her golden eyes. "Why, to congratulate you, of course! Word spreads quickly around here, [pc.name]; given the unique nature of your induction into the Order Astrida, it only seemed natural that I should offer you some personal congratulations! I was hoping you'd arrive sometime soon, and here you are!"
    
    As much as you're caught off-guard, you recover quickly. Thanking Lystra, she nods her head, and steps back. Returning to her seat, Lystra shuffles a few papers, before returning her gaze to you politely.
    
    "Now then, dear, was there anything you had needed from me?"

rows.translation: 你花了一点时间观察那位身形像鹰、面容像女人的图书管理员，然后在她对面的位置坐了下来。首先吸引你注意的，当然是莱斯特拉的不同她看起来和你们见过的任何女妖都不一样。 [dayNight |她戴着一副大框眼镜，镜片厚得是你见过的最厚的了。透过那些镜片，两只金色的大眼睛闪烁着光芒，但由于她夜行性的生活习惯，她的双眼总是半闭着，微微眯着。 |她闲暇时翻阅着一本小册子，显然，莱斯特拉更像是个夜猫子——与白天那个昏昏欲睡、话少得可怜的图书管理员截然不同，此刻的她更像是一位热心的学者。她甚至没有借助蜡烛阅读，那厚厚的眼镜使得她金色的眼睛显得更加大了。 ]她的成熟程度也远高于普通的鹰身女妖——看起来就像一位四十岁左右的人类女性，按照鹰身女妖的标准来说，她确实属于年纪较大的一类。不过，除此之外，你很快就会注意到，莱斯特拉的颜色和羽毛也显得非常独特。与那些通常被阳轻型晒成古铜色的鹰身女妖们相比，她的皮肤苍白而柔软，这显然说明她并不像大多数同类那样经常待在户外。此外，她的“头发”也有些与众不同：棕褐色的羽毛覆盖着她的头部，而那些特殊的绒毛使她的“头发”看起来像是一个松散的发髻。在你见过的所有鹰身女妖中，她与众不同——她的肩膀和脖子上覆盖着一层柔软的羽毛，还有一条短而宽的鸟尾。她的翅膀和腿部也同样长满了羽毛，这些羽毛又宽又蓬松，触感十分柔软，而她手部和足部上那些凶恶的爪子，则与这些羽毛形成了鲜明的对比。尽管动作敏捷，但莱斯特拉的手部法却轻柔而细腻，翻动书页时动作娴熟而从容。 然而，第二个同样会吸引你注意的特征，便是她的身材。 莱斯特拉身材粗壮结实，身高大约为五英尺八英寸——这显然比大多数当地的蝾螈要短得多。看来，莱斯特拉的生长过程似乎与其他蝾螈有所不同。出局而不是向上，这个假设因为她那丰满的身材而显得更加可信。两个巨大的 [lystra.isMom |乳白色的 |悬挂的；摇摆的 ] 她的毛衣将胸部衬托得格外饱满，每一个乳晕都足以容纳莱斯特拉的整个头部，甚至还有剩余。乍一看，这个露出的胸部轮廓似乎显得极为挑逗，但莱斯特拉却只觉得这不过是多了一个口袋而已；她完全没有意识到，将自己的卷轴夹在胸前，其实会带来多么引人注目的效果。 [lystra.isMom |考虑到它们的体积如此庞大，阿尔巴总是喜欢依偎在这些东西旁边也就不足为奇了……说起来，你女儿压在它们上面的重量似乎让莱斯特拉再次开始渗液了。在那件羊毛衫的正面，可以看到两处散发着淡淡甜味的潮湿痕迹，不过莱斯特拉似乎还没有注意到这一情况。 |说起来，她的体形确实没有那些女妖般丰满，但丰满的胸部在女妖群体中确实算是比较少见的现象。不禁让人好奇，她究竟是怎么做到的飞行身上挂着那些东西 ]在下面部分，情况也差不多。莱斯特拉那朴素的装束并没有过多地展示她的身材，但 [lystra.fucked |你知道下面到底是什么吧 |她那柔美的曲线使得即使她穿着普通的衣服，也足以激发人们的想象力。 ]. [lystra.pregStage 0 2 |她那柔软、圆润的…… |她那圆润、仿佛孕育着生命的身体…… ] [silly |箱子；储物箱 |中部区域 ] 从她的裙子上可以清楚地看到这一点，而那些典型的、像鹰头女妖一样宽大的臀部也丝毫没有被忽略。 [lystra.fucked |当然，鉴于你与莱斯特拉共度的那些经历，你肯定非常清楚她的穿着打扮是怎样的。确实隐藏起来吧。你肯定知道她的臀部有多么丰满诱人——厚厚的脂肪层与柔软的绒毛交织在一起，巧妙地掩盖了那些用于助跑起飞的强健腿部肌肉，从而使莱斯特拉拥有了一对堪称“完美”的大腿“靠垫”。[lystra.isMom | 毫不奇怪，生完孩子后，她的大腿变得更加丰满结实了——每一条大腿都比你的头还要粗，其柔软的脂肪组织足以让你的手陷了进去，而她那变宽的臀部更是让大腿的体积显得更加突出。 | ] 此外，与她的大腿一样，莱斯特拉紧致轻型滑的阴部也覆盖着一层柔软的绒毛——那是一丛蓬松的小绒毛。 | ] 尽管身材魁梧，但莱斯特拉的实际灵活性却出人意料。她行动敏捷，常常能在几乎无声无息的情况下突然移动，就像一只真正的猫头鹰一样——她在飞行时发出的唯一声响，也只是轻微的重击在着陆后，她的行走方式也几乎看不出来有什么不同；她的动作非常轻柔。咔嗒咔嗒声她移动时总会挥动着自己的利爪，但她的潜行能力实在无人能及——她总能不知不觉地接近目标。没人知道她是怎么做到的，但生活总有些神秘之处吧……对于在图书馆工作的人来说，这种能力无疑是非常宝贵的。总的来说，用来形容莱斯特拉的最恰当词语，恐怕就是“充满母性关怀”。 [lystra.isMom |而且不仅仅是字面意义上的那样； |即便不考虑她的外貌， ] 在大教堂里，她就像一位善良而充满关怀的存在，乐于帮助学者们和朝圣者们。 [lystra.isMom |当然，她怀里还抱着那个可爱的小宝宝。你的宝宝。[lystra.numKids 1 2 | | 最年长的 ] 女儿阿尔巴 [dayNight |她依偎在母亲的胸前，正沉沉地睡着呢。 |从莱斯特拉的腿上探出头来，暂时停止了她的写作练习。 ]由于鹰头鹫的成长速度如此之快，她现在已经有了人类幼儿般的体型，而且也同样有着强烈的求知欲。这个充满好奇心的小猫头鹰每当妈妈给她读书时，都会迫不及待地跟着学习。虽然她那连绵不断的问题可能会让人感到有些烦扰，但想到自己培养出了这样一个如此渴望学习的女儿，心中还是会感到无比自豪的。她的身臂和腿部都覆盖着柔软、绒毛般的羽毛，这些羽毛与她母亲的羽毛十分相似，只不过她的羽毛是柔和的灰色，而莱斯特拉的羽毛则是棕色的。虽然她的翅膀还没有发育到可以飞行的程度，但她无疑继承了莱斯特拉那种轻巧敏捷的体质——毫无疑问，她很快就会用自己的出现把大教堂里的访客们吓一跳的。 [dayNight |你注视着她熟睡的样子，观察着她呼吸时胸膛的轻轻起伏。毫无疑问，她此刻一定在梦里聆听母亲给她读过的那些书…… |当你注视着阿尔巴时，她正从莱斯特拉的膝上朝你微笑，然后又继续她之前的工作——把听到的单词记录下来。真是个学习能力很强的孩子啊…… ] | ]

rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_LIBRARY |Thinking on a topic, you decide to ask Lystra about [rand |her time working with the library. Does she enjoy it? Lystra [dayNight |gives a soft smile |smiles warmly ] as you ask, visibly thinking back to pleasant memories, before replying. "[dayNight |Hoo... yes, I do enjoy it |Ah, yes. I've always loved my time here ]. I've been enamored with the cathedral's archives ever since I was a chick. I distinctly recall one evening, when my father brought me along to retrieve a scroll he wished to peruse; I fell in love the moment I walked in. I spent much of my free time here, simply learning for the sake of learning; by the time I was fully grown, I knew this was what I wished to devote my life to." Lystra gently smiles as she reminisces, the twinkle of old memories in her golden eyes. So, how did she come to work here? She mentioned that Eirina somewhat abruptly placed her in charge recently, but what about before that? Lystra [dayNight |blinks in surprise, somewhat embarrassed |clears her throat, chuckling softly before she responds ]. "Well, I, ah... I asked. It must have been... oh, nearly twenty years ago now, when I did. I still remember it, mostly because it was so uncouth of me..." She adjusts her position in the chair, avoiding your gaze somewhat. "If I'm to continue, you must promise me not to laugh. I'm getting embarrassed just remembering this, you know." [pc.isDK |Do you have to? |Seriously? It can't be that bad. ] "I'm serious, dear." Lystra retorts, uncharacteristically stern. [pc.isDK |Fine, fine. Y |So be it; y ]ou promise. "Very well, then. As I was saying... one morning, I marched my way up to the front desk, and pleaded my case to lady Evadne, the previous Lorekeeper. She greeted me the same as she always did, and then, well... I begged to be able to work at the cathedral, to help others who pursued learning as I did... I said I'd do anything, make any vow, whatever it took. And when I looked up at Evadne... she was absolutely mortified." Lystra buries her neck in her fluffy collar for a moment, before continuing. "She said that I didn't have to beg, swear, or do anything; that she knew exactly how much I loved to learn, to help others to learn, and that she wouldn't dream of denying me that. And then, she said the worst part of all. That they were always accepting applicants, and I could have just taken a form from the desk." ...Wow. That is pretty embarrassing. Lystra mumbles something under her breath, then clears her throat and looks back at you. "All the same, that's the past, and this is now. In the nineteen or so years since, I've learned much, and I've loved every moment of helping the scholars and visitors to this place. I certainly never expected to be placed in charge of it, though– even temporarily." Sounds like she quite enjoys working here. |her duties to the library. What is it that she does here? Lystra takes a second to consider your question, before lifting a wing and gesturing at the enormous scroll-shelves around the cathedral. "[dayNight |Allll of this |What you see all around you ] is what I do here, dear. From my first day on the job, my duties have been the maintaining of the archives. While the shelves may appear disorderly and assorted at a glance, I can assure you that there is a system– one of my own invention. Wait, she sorts all the scrolls and tomes in the archives? How can she even manage that? Lystra gives a prideful smirk in response, clearly reveling in the indirect praise. "Well, I did, before Eirina placed me in charge, at least. It wasn't all my own work, either; the library's numerical cataloging system was the result of much effort between myself and Lorekeeper Evadne, Eirina's predecessor. Prior to its creation, our inventory was sorted variously by both order of acquisition, and the author responsible; a very confusing mixture." But how does she physically manage to do that? Between retrieval and return, you can't imagine she has the idle time to do much else. "[dayNight |Mm, well..." Lystra yawns, taking a moment to stretch her wings as she does so. " |Ah, well, ]I did specify that I did that prior to assuming leadership. Sleeping during the day can be helpful when the library is much slower at night; I would often spend the night returning the day's work back to its home. rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_HERSELF |Thinking on possible topics, you settle on [rand |Lystra's family. She mentioned her mother raised her; what is she like? Lystra smiles softly at your question, a kind expression as nods her head. "As a matter of fact, my mother and father have both been there to raise me. I’m well aware that’s quite uncommon for harpies; though, the way they met is certainly more of what you may expect." Oh? "You see, my mother used to be a thief, though not the sort of banditry common among the harpies of the Marches. Back when she was a young, scrawny thing, she happened upon my father’s merchant-cart one night, and swooped down to grab a bundle of food... and instead fetched a very frightened salamander with a bad habit of sleeping on his merchandise. From the way I heard it, his companions managed to wrestle her to the ground, and asked my father what to do with her." Lystra chuckles softly before she resumes. "Rather than truss her up and leave her, or exact a... carnal sort of revenge, or do something even more nefarious, he simply said to get some food from one of the packs and give it to her, then leave her be. According to her, that simple act of kindness won her heart." And then? "She followed him for days. He told his companions not to drive her off, but to let her keep following from a distance. He'd leave spare rations out for her, and she'd swipe them every night. One morning, just before the dawn, she approached my father's sleeping pack, leaned down, and said, quite bluntly, that she loved him." [pc.isDK |Good lord, you think you're going to gag |...Wow ]. "I know, right?" Lystra agrees, laughing. "The two of them were inseparable after that. She stuck with him for the remainder of his travels, and eventually moved to Tychris with him when he returned. I was born soon after, and my sister followed a year later. The three of them still run a store down in the city, and I visit often." Sounds like she had it pretty good, then. "Oh, absolutely. I'd be a fool not to see how fortunate I've been in life.[lystra.isMom | Furthermore, I know Alba here will have all three of them to rely on for support as well as you and I. I couldn't be happier with the way things have turned out." |" ] Lystra smiles warmly at you, then clears her throat gently. "So, was there anything else you wished to speak about?" |Lystra's interests. What is it that she likes to do? Lystra [dayNight |blinks confusedly a few times, as if not understanding the question |Stares at you for a few moments, confused ]. "Well... I like to read. That much should be a fairly obvious inference, given my choice of career. Aside from that, though..." Lystra scratches her chin, deep in thought. "Hmm. I suppose one could say my interests are quite narrow, actually. I mean, I quite enjoy reading to others as well; I often do so for the young Astrida, as well as the children of the other staff. [lystra.isMom |Of course, that also includes ours." Lystra adds, gently stroking Alba on the head. " | ]I quite enjoy doing that– to learn is to improve oneself, and one should always aim ever upwards. Helping the latest generation to do so is the greatest joy one can attain." [pc.dcb |So she just sits in the library and reads all day? You can't imagine doing something so boring all day. What does she even read? |What is it that she reads in particular, though? She must have a favorite subject. |Ugh... that must be, like, soooo many books. Are they, like, at least about fun stuff? ] Lystra's eyes light up at your question, visibly excited. "[pc.dcb |Oh, everything! But |Of course! I read a bit of everything, but |The most fun of all! What I read is ] mostly classical literature. In my youth however, I avidly read magical theory. I'm no mage, myself– I never had the knack for it, but it was a profoundly interesting field to me all the same." What spurred her to switch subjects? [dayNight |Lystra frowns a bit, then begins softly gesturing around the room at the enormous shelves of scrolls |Lystra chuckles dryly — an unusual note of sarcasm from her, then begins gesturing at the towering scroll-shelves throughout the library ]. "Do you see all of these scrolls, tomes, and tablets, [pc.name]? I could learn every spell emblazoned upon them, teach myself the mechanics behind each and every minute detail, and by the time I would think I had mastered them, I would be over a century past my lifespan. And this is just what we make publicly accessible. I am, unfortunately, a perfectionist with magic; so much so that it's a detriment. The skill I lacked for magic was composure; I'd panic the moment any detail went awry. That's chiefly why I gave up on it; it interests me still, but there would be no use in learning it. Knowledge you never use may as well be forgotten, for all the good it does you." Lystra lowers her wing, and her warm smile returns as she meets your gaze once more. "Of course, those are simply my own personal foibles. Reading the works of authors long gone is merely something I can derive greater personal satisfaction from, and thus, it is what I chose to pursue. At any rate: was there anything else you wished to inquire about?" |Lystra's personal life. What’s she got going on in her day-to-day? Lystra [lystra.isMom |[dayNight |gives you a quizzical look, amplified further by her drowsiness |laughs softly, amused by the directness of the question ]. Taking a moment before she begins to gesture at Alba, she meets your eyes with a bemused expression. "Well, as of recently, quite a bit is going on in my life, [pc.name]. I should think you were aware of that much already, but I know what you meant. Alba's been quite the handful lately, but I still have my duties to uphold. Once the... situation with the Order is resolved, I think I may take some personal time, let her properly have some family time with her aunt and grandparents. Aside from that however, things are mostly the same as it ever was. [silly |Letting the days go by, and whatnot |Another day, another night, more of the same ]. Not that I mind, of course. There's something to be said for consistency and routine, after all. Between Alba [lystra.numKids 1 2 |and |as well as the others, plus ] my extra duties, my hands are quite full, so my own hobbies have made their way to the sidelines given the circumstances." What about any other happenings in her life? Lystra laughs softly, meeting your gaze directly. "Well, aside from a certain someone recently becoming the apple of my eye, not much else has changed– at least in my work life." Lystra gives you a slight wink at that, before leaning back into her chair a bit. "Though, now that you mention it, I have noticed that nobody's... well, made a pass at me in a while. Gods, to think, for all those years, everyone might have been serious..." [pc.isDK |The way you see it, if they didn't have the strength of will to keep trying like you did, they didn't deserve someone like her |It's unfortunate, but you're certainly not going to complain about how things turned out; you're glad to be the one Lystra loves. ]. Lystra gives you a warm smile, her face lightening in response. "Why, thank you, [pc.name]. It means a lot to me to hear you say that. At any rate, however, we ought to save the bedroom talk for the bedroom. Was there anything else you wished to discuss?" |[dayNight |nods softly |leans back in her chair a bit ] as she listens to your question, before replying. "Mm... not all that much, to tell the truth. I am, admittedly, rather a plain woman. I'm quite busy with my duties to the library lately, and as such, my free time has been playing second fiddle to that for a while now. Not that I mind, though. I've dedicated my life towards this library, and being asked to maintain it as the head, even temporarily, is an incredible honor." [pc.isDK |So she's content to just waste her life away in a dusty old library |She doesn't mind sacrificing her personal time like that ]? Lystra frowns a bit, tilting her head at you as she hears that. "No, I wouldn't quite say that. It's simply that I understand the circumstances must be dire for such a task to fall upon a humble acolyte like myself, and harbor no objections to the will of the Goddess. It's not like I'm missing out on all that much, anyhow– aside from [lystra.fucked |a certain someone becoming the apple of my eye recently |the occasional scholar or Astrida asking me on a date as a prank ], I don't have much going on in my life. [lystra.fucked |Speaking of which, how's the tide of 'joking' suitors been for her lately? Lystra blushes a bit, burying her neck into her collar of down before she replies. "They, um... well, word spreads rather quickly around these parts, and they've uh... stopped." Lystra tilts her eyes downwards, before she continues. "G-gods, I'm still embarrassed about that... and rather remorseful, too. I must have broken so many young hearts inadvertently..." ...You can imagine that someone a bit less persistent than you probably wouldn't take it too well when she started laughing about it, yes. Lystra all but squawks in distress, before composing herself. "Ahem. At any rate, this is hardly a topic to discuss publicly. What else did you wish to speak about? |...As a prank? Lystra snickers a little bit, covering her mouth with a wing. "Hoo... yes, of course. I mean, it's so patently absurd! I suspect it's some sort of hazing ritual amongst the newly-training Astrida: a test of courage, perhaps. 'Oh, you think you're brave? Why don't you go ask the old lady for a date, then?' It's the only plausible reason why they do it year after year. In fact, they're probably the ones daring scholars to do it, as well." Lystra laughs, her hearty chuckles resembling a soft hooting sound. Has she ever considered that some of them might not have been joking? Lystra begins to laugh even harder at that, nearly doubling over in her chair as she does so. "Hoo-hoo-hoo, [pc.name], please! I'm just an old lady working at a library, not some Mallachite icon! There's nothing about an old girl like me that those youngsters could seriously consider attractive." Lystra guffaws, and you're treated to the sight of [silly |those fat fucking owl tits |her enormous chest ] bouncing and jiggling as she does. Right, nothing at all... "Hoo... at any rate, [pc.name], I should thank you for the laugh. Was there anything else you wished to speak about?" ] ] ] |You've got to ask: What's the deal with Lystra, exactly? You've never seen a harpy like her before. Her features are much more owl-like, compared to the usual, more broadly-avian characteristics of harpies– does she know anything about that? If Lystra's response is anything to go off of, she must get asked that question often. Softly laughing, she gently shakes her head in amusement, before removing her glasses to look at you directly. "[dayNight |Hoo... it seems everyone asks that eventually |Well, I suppose that was to be expected ]. Yes, I'm aware my appearance is rather... unique, at least for the area. As I'm sure is perfectly obvious, I am a harpy, albeit not from the Frost Marches. Or rather, my kin are not; I was born here. To answer your question, however, yes. A topic I pursued with avid curiosity in my youth was my own nature, constantly bombarding my mother with questions about where we were from." [dayNight |Lystra's half-lidded eyes have the warmth of old memories in them |Lystra smiles fondly, relishing old memories ] as she continues. "To answer somewhat bluntly, it turns out my mother hails from Claremont, originally; she traveled quite far alongside my father to end up here." Lystra pauses for a moment, before lifting a wing to show her feathers. Pointing at various spots, she continues on. "The differences between us and the harpies native to this area are pronounced, as I'm sure you've noticed. You're correct in the sentiment that I resemble an owl; they share many of the same adaptations. The foremost divergence is actually our plumage: the structure of our feathers means that, while harpies like myself fly slower, we can do so nearly silently." You imagine that must be helpful in a library of all places. [dayNight |Very much so. I'd demonstrate, but I'm quite tired at the moment... that said, |Lystra smiles proudly, brimming over with childlike glee. "I know, isn't it? You'd think it was a blessing from Sorra herself! Though, given the usual proclivities of harpies, it's more likely an adaptation to be more effe– ah." Lystra catches herself, clearing her throat before regaining her composure. "Pardon the excitement, [pc.name], I was getting a bit carried away. To recenter our discussion, ] there are a few other traits that are different as compared to the harpies you're likely familiar with. We actually have tails, though they're largely vestigial, and we keep our down feathers from our time as chicks; those two features are more minor, but they are distinctive. At any rate, I believe I've answered your question; was there anything else?" ]
rows.translation: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_HERSELF |在思考可能的主题后，你最终确定了某个方向。 [rand |莱斯特拉的家人。她提到是她的母亲抚养了她，那她的母亲是个怎样的人呢？ 莱斯特拉听到你的问题，轻轻地笑了起来，脸上带着亲切的表情，然后点了点头说道：“其实，我的母亲以及我的父母都尽心尽力地抚养我长大。我很清楚，对于女妖族来说，这种情况其实相当罕见；不过，他们相识的方式，倒确实符合人们的预期。 哦？ “你知道的，我母亲曾经是个小偷，不过并不是那种在边境地区常见的女妖盗贼。当初她还只是个瘦小的小家伙的时候，有天晚上她偶然发现了我父亲的商贩马车，立刻飞过去抓了一捆食物……结果却抓到了一只非常害怕的蝾螈，这只蝾螈有个坏习惯，总喜欢把东西当成枕头来睡。据我听说的，他的同伴们把她摔倒在地，然后问我的父亲该如何处置她。莱斯特拉轻声笑了笑，继续说道：“他没有选择把她绑起来丢弃，也没有采取什么残忍的报复手段，甚至没有做出更恶劣的事情。他只是让人从背包里拿些食物给她，然后让她离开。据她所说，那个简单的善举赢得了她的心。 然后呢？ “她跟随了他天数他告诉同伴们不要把她赶走，而是让她在远处继续跟着。他会留一些多余的口粮给她，而她每晚都会来拿。一天清晨，在黎明之前，她走到我父亲的睡袋旁，俯下身来，直截了当地对他说，她爱他。 [pc.isDK |天啊，你真以为自己会吐出来的吗？ |哇…… ]我知道对吧？”莱斯特拉笑着同意道，“从那以后，他们俩就形影不离了。在他接下来的旅途中，她一直陪伴着他，等他回到蒂克里斯后，她也跟着搬了过去。不久之后我就出生了，我的姐姐则在一年后出生。他们三个现在还在城里开了一家店，我经常去拜访他们。” 听起来她的生活过得相当不错啊。 “哦，当然了。如果我不认识到自己这一生有多幸运，那才真是太傻了呢。[lystra.isMom | 此外，我知道在这里的阿尔巴也会像你和我一样，可以依靠这三个人来获得支持。对于事情的发展结果，我再满意不过了。 |" ] 莱斯特拉向你温暖地笑了笑，然后轻轻清了清嗓子。 “那么，还有其他你想谈论的事情吗？ |莱斯特拉的兴趣爱好。她喜欢做些什么呢？ [dayNight |他困惑地眨了几下眼，似乎并不理解这个问题。 |愣愣地盯着你看了一会儿，显得十分困惑。 ]嗯……我喜欢阅读。考虑到我选择的职业，这一点应该很容易被理解吧。不过，除此之外……”莱斯特拉挠了挠下巴，陷入了沉思。“嗯，我想可以说，我的兴趣其实相当狭窄。也就是说，我真的很喜欢阅读。向其他人也是这样；我经常为年轻的阿斯特里达以及其他员工的孩子们做这件事。 [lystra.isMom |当然，这也包括我们的。”莱斯特拉轻声说道，同时轻轻抚摸着阿尔巴的头部。 | ]我非常喜欢这样做——学习就是自我提升，人应该始终追求进步。能够帮助新一代人实现这一目标，便是我能获得的最大快乐。 [pc.dcb |所以她就整天坐在图书馆里读书吗？你简直无法想象整天做这么无聊的事情。她到底读些什么书呢？ |不过，她具体在读些什么呢？她肯定有自己最喜欢的科目吧。 |呃……那些书肯定有非常多吧。它们至少应该是关于……什么的吧？有趣什么玩意儿？ ] 听到你的问题，莱斯特拉的眼睛亮了起来，显然非常兴奋。[pc.dcb |哦，所有事情！但是…… |当然！我什么类型的书都读过一些，不过…… |其中最有趣的部分！我读到的内容是…… ] 主要是阅读古典文学作品。然而在我年轻的时候，我非常热衷于研究魔法理论。虽然我自己并不是法师——我从来都没有那种天赋——但这个领域确实让我感到非常着迷。那么，是什么促使她改变了研究方向呢？ [dayNight |莱斯特拉微微皱了皱眉头，然后开始轻轻地在房间里指着那些摆满卷轴的巨大书架示意着什么。 |莱斯特拉干笑了一声——这种带有讽刺意味的笑声在她身上实属罕见，然后她开始指着图书馆里那些高耸的卷轴架示意起来。 ]你看到这些卷轴、典籍和石板了吗？ [pc.name]我可以学会它们上面记载的每一个法术，自己研究其中每一个细节背后的原理。而当我以为自己已经完全掌握了这些法术时，我的寿命其实已经超过了一个世纪。而这就是我们创造出来的东西。公开地可塑性。不幸的是，我在魔法方面是个完美主义者，这种特质反而成了我的障碍。我在魔法学习中缺乏的，正是这种可塑性。冷静沉着只要有任何细节出错，我就会惊慌失措。这也是我最终放弃它的原因；虽然它仍然让我感兴趣，但学习它也没有任何意义。那些你从未使用过的知识，还不如忘掉它们，因为它们根本不会给你带来任何好处。莱斯特拉放下她的翅膀，当她再次与你的目轻型相遇时，她那温暖的笑容重新浮现。“当然，那些只不过是我个人的爱好罢了。阅读那些早已离世的作家的作品，只是让我能获得更大的个人满足感，因此，这也是我选择去追求的事情。无论如何：还有其他你想了解的事情吗？ |莱斯特拉的私人生活。她的日常生活中究竟发生了些什么呢？ [lystra.isMom |[dayNight |她用一种充满疑惑的眼神看着你，而她的困倦更是让这种神情显得更加明显。 |轻声笑了起来，被这个直率的问题逗乐了。 ]她停顿了一下，然后开始朝阿尔巴示意，同时用一种困惑的表情看着你：“嗯，最近我的生活中发生了很多事情 [pc.name]我想你应该已经知道这些了，但我明白你的意思。最近阿尔巴确实让人有些头疼，但我仍然有我的职责要履行。等……与那个组织的矛盾解决了，我想我就可以抽一些时间，让她能够和她的阿姨以及祖父母好好地共度一些家庭时轻型。不过除此之外，一切还是和以前一样。 [silly |日子就这样一天天过去了。 |又一天，又一个夜晚，一切依旧如故。 ]当然，我并不介意。毕竟，一致性与规律性也有其可取之处。在阿尔巴之间 [lystra.numKids 1 2 |以及 |还有其他一些，再加上…… ] 由于还有其他额外的工作要处理，我的手部实在忙不过来，因此在这种情况下，我的个人爱好也就被搁在了一边。” 那么，她生活中还发生了其他什么事情呢？ 莱斯特拉轻声笑了起来，直视着你的眼睛回答道。嗯，除了有某个人最近成了我心中的宝贝之外，其他方面并没有什么变化——至少在我的工作生活中是这样。”莱斯特拉说着朝你眨了眨眼，然后稍微向后靠在椅子上。“不过，既然你提到了这个拥有我注意到，已经有好一阵子没有人……嗯，对我表示过兴趣了。天啊，想想看，这么多年来，也许所有人都是认真的 [pc.isDK |在你看来，如果他们没有像你那样坚持不懈的毅力，那么他们就不配拥有她这样的人。 |虽然有些遗憾，但你肯定不会抱怨事情的结果吧？你能成为莱斯特拉所爱的人，你应该感到高兴才对。 ]莱斯特拉向你露出了温暖的微笑，她的脸上洋溢着喜悦。“哦，谢谢你。 [pc.name]听到你这么说，对我来说意义重大。无论如何，我们还是应该把那些私密的话题留在卧室里讨论。还有其他你想聊的事情吗？ |[dayNight |轻轻点了点头 |她在椅子上稍微向后靠了靠。 ] 当她听到你的问题时，她先沉思了一会儿，然后回答道：“嗯……说实话，也没那么多时间。我确实算是个相貌普通的女性。最近我忙于履行在图书馆的职责，因此我的空闲时间都被这些工作占去了。不过我并不介意，因为我把一生都奉献给了这个图书馆。能够被邀请担任馆长，哪怕只是暂时的，对我来说也是一种无上的荣誉。 [pc.isDK |偶尔会有学者或者像阿斯特里达这样的朋友开玩笑地约我出去约会。 ]我的生活中并没有太多事情发生。 [lystra.fucked |说到这个，最近那些“开玩笑”地追求她的男士们，情况怎么样呢？ 莱斯特拉微微脸红，把脖子埋进羽绒领子里，然后回答道：“他们啊……嗯，这边消息传得还挺快的，所以他们…………然后就停了下来。”莱斯特拉低下头，继续说道：“天啊，我到现在仍然为那件事感到羞愧……也充满了懊悔。我肯定无意中伤害了很多年轻人的心……你可以想象，如果有人没有你这么坚持，当她开始拿这件事开玩笑时，她很可能不会接受得很好，没错。 莱斯特拉先是急得几乎尖叫起来，后来才慢慢平静下来。 rows.raw: " [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_HERSELF |Thinking on possible topics, you settle on [rand |Lystra's family. She mentioned her mother raised her; what is she like? Lystra smiles softly at your question, a kind expression as nods her head. "As a matter of fact, my mother and father have both been there to raise me. I’m well aware that’s quite uncommon for harpies; though, the way they met is certainly more of what you may expect." Oh? "You see, my mother used to be a thief, though not the sort of banditry common among the harpies of the Marches. Back when she was a young, scrawny thing, she happened upon my father’s merchant-cart one night, and swooped down to grab a bundle of food... and instead fetched a very frightened salamander with a bad habit of sleeping on his merchandise. From the way I heard it, his companions managed to wrestle her to the ground, and asked my father what to do with her." Lystra chuckles softly before she resumes. "Rather than truss her up and leave her, or exact a... carnal sort of revenge, or do something even more nefarious, he simply said to get some food from one of the packs and give it to her, then leave her be. According to her, that simple act of kindness won her heart." And then? "She followed him for days. He told his companions not to drive her off, but to let her keep following from a distance. He'd leave spare rations out for her, and she'd swipe them every night. One morning, just before the dawn, she approached my father's sleeping pack, leaned down, and said, quite bluntly, that she loved him." [pc.isDK |Good lord, you think you're going to gag |...Wow ]. "I know, right?" Lystra agrees, laughing. "The two of them were inseparable after that. She stuck with him for the remainder of his travels, and eventually moved to Tychris with him when he returned. I was born soon after, and my sister followed a year later. The three of them still run a store down in the city, and I visit often." Sounds like she had it pretty good, then. "Oh, absolutely. I'd be a fool not to see how fortunate I've been in life.[lystra.isMom | Furthermore, I know Alba here will have all three of them to rely on for support as well as you and I. I couldn't be happier with the way things have turned out." |" ] Lystra smiles warmly at you, then clears her throat gently. "So, was there anything else you wished to speak about?" |Lystra's interests. What is it that she likes to do? Lystra [dayNight |blinks confusedly a few times, as if not understanding the question |Stares at you for a few moments, confused ]. "Well... I like to read. That much should be a fairly obvious inference, given my choice of career. Aside from that, though..." Lystra scratches her chin, deep in thought. "Hmm. I suppose one could say my interests are quite narrow, actually. I mean, I quite enjoy reading to others as well; I often do so for the young Astrida, as well as the children of the other staff. [lystra.isMom |Of course, that also includes ours." Lystra adds, gently stroking Alba on the head. " | ]I quite enjoy doing that– to learn is to improve oneself, and one should always aim ever upwards. Helping the latest generation to do so is the greatest joy one can attain." [pc.dcb |So she just sits in the library and reads all day? You can't imagine doing something so boring all day. What does she even read? |What is it that she reads in particular, though? She must have a favorite subject. |Ugh... that must be, like, soooo many books. Are they, like, at least about fun stuff? ] Lystra's eyes light up at your question, visibly excited. "[pc.dcb |Oh, everything! But |Of course! I read a bit of everything, but |The most fun of all! What I read is ] mostly classical literature. In my youth however, I avidly read magical theory. I'm no mage, myself– I never had the knack for it, but it was a profoundly interesting field to me all the same." What spurred her to switch subjects? [dayNight |Lystra frowns a bit, then begins softly gesturing around the room at the enormous shelves of scrolls |Lystra chuckles dryly — an unusual note of sarcasm from her, then begins gesturing at the towering scroll-shelves throughout the library ]. "Do you see all of these scrolls, tomes, and tablets, [pc.name]? I could learn every spell emblazoned upon them, teach myself the mechanics behind each and every minute detail, and by the time I would think I had mastered them, I would be over a century past my lifespan. And this is just what we make publicly accessible. I am, unfortunately, a perfectionist with magic; so much so that it's a detriment. The skill I lacked for magic was composure; I'd panic the moment any detail went awry. That's chiefly why I gave up on it; it interests me still, but there would be no use in learning it. Knowledge you never use may as well be forgotten, for all the good it does you." Lystra lowers her wing, and her warm smile returns as she meets your gaze once more. "Of course, those are simply my own personal foibles. Reading the works of authors long gone is merely something I can derive greater personal satisfaction from, and thus, it is what I chose to pursue. At any rate: was there anything else you wished to inquire about?" |Lystra's personal life. What’s she got going on in her day-to-day? Lystra [lystra.isMom |[dayNight |gives you a quizzical look, amplified further by her drowsiness |laughs softly, amused by the directness of the question ]. Taking a moment before she begins to gesture at Alba, she meets your eyes with a bemused expression. "Well, as of recently, quite a bit is going on in my life, [pc.name]. I should think you were aware of that much already, but I know what you meant. Alba's been quite the handful lately, but I still have my duties to uphold. Once the... situation with the Order is resolved, I think I may take some personal time, let her properly have some family time with her aunt and grandparents. Aside from that however, things are mostly the same as it ever was. [silly |Letting the days go by, and whatnot |Another day, another night, more of the same ]. Not that I mind, of course. There's something to be said for consistency and routine, after all. Between Alba [lystra.numKids 1 2 |and |as well as the others, plus ] my extra duties, my hands are quite full, so my own hobbies have made their way to the sidelines given the circumstances." What about any other happenings in her life? Lystra laughs softly, meeting your gaze directly. "Well, aside from a certain someone recently becoming the apple of my eye, not much else has changed– at least in my work life." Lystra gives you a slight wink at that, before leaning back into her chair a bit. "Though, now that you mention it, I have noticed that nobody's... well, made a pass at me in a while. Gods, to think, for all those years, everyone might have been serious..." [pc.isDK |The way you see it, if they didn't have the strength of will to keep trying like you did, they didn't deserve someone like her |It's unfortunate, but you're certainly not going to complain about how things turned out; you're glad to be the one Lystra loves. ]. Lystra gives you a warm smile, her face lightening in response. "Why, thank you, [pc.name]. It means a lot to me to hear you say that. At any rate, however, we ought to save the bedroom talk for the bedroom. Was there anything else you wished to discuss?" |[dayNight |nods softly |leans back in her chair a bit ] as she listens to your question, before replying. "Mm... not all that much, to tell the truth. I am, admittedly, rather a plain woman. I'm quite busy with my duties to the library lately, and as such, my free time has been playing second fiddle to that for a while now. Not that I mind, though. I've dedicated my life towards this library, and being asked to maintain it as the head, even temporarily, is an incredible honor." [pc.isDK |So she's content to just waste her life away in a dusty old library |She doesn't mind sacrificing her personal time like that ]? Lystra frowns a bit, tilting her head at you as she hears that. "No, I wouldn't quite say that. It's simply that I understand the circumstances must be dire for such a task to fall upon a humble acolyte like myself, and harbor no objections to the will of the Goddess. It's not like I'm missing out on all that much, anyhow– aside from [lystra.fucked |a certain someone becoming the apple of my eye recently |the occasional scholar or Astrida asking me on a date as a prank ], I don't have much going on in my life. [lystra.fucked |Speaking of which, how's the tide of 'joking' suitors been for her lately? Lystra blushes a bit, burying her neck into her collar of down before she replies. "They, um... well, word spreads rather quickly around these parts, and they've uh... stopped." Lystra tilts her eyes downwards, before she continues. "G-gods, I'm still embarrassed about that... and rather remorseful, too. I must have broken so many young hearts inadvertently..." ...You can imagine that someone a bit less persistent than you probably wouldn't take it too well when she started laughing about it, yes. Lystra all but squawks in distress, before composing herself. "Ahem. At any rate, this is hardly a topic to discuss publicly. What else did you wish to speak about? |...As a prank? Lystra snickers a little bit, covering her mouth with a wing. "Hoo... yes, of course. I mean, it's so patently absurd! I suspect it's some sort of hazing ritual amongst the newly-training Astrida: a test of courage, perhaps. 'Oh, you think you're brave? Why don't you go ask the old lady for a date, then?' It's the only plausible reason why they do it year after year. In fact, they're probably the ones daring scholars to do it, as well." Lystra laughs, her hearty chuckles resembling a soft hooting sound. Has she ever considered that some of them might not have been joking? Lystra begins to laugh even harder at that, nearly doubling over in her chair as she does so. "Hoo-hoo-hoo, [pc.name], please! I'm just an old lady working at a library, not some Mallachite icon! There's nothing about an old girl like me that those youngsters could seriously consider attractive." Lystra guffaws, and you're treated to the sight of [silly |those fat fucking owl tits |her enormous chest ] bouncing and jiggling as she does. Right, nothing at all... "Hoo... at any rate, [pc.name], I should thank you for the laugh. Was there anything else you wished to speak about?" ] ] ] |You've got to ask: What's the deal with Lystra, exactly? You've never seen a harpy like her before. Her features are much more owl-like, compared to the usual, more broadly-avian characteristics of harpies– does she know anything about that? If Lystra's response is anything to go off of, she must get asked that question often. Softly laughing, she gently shakes her head in amusement, before removing her glasses to look at you directly. "[dayNight |Hoo... it seems everyone asks that eventually |Well, I suppose that was to be expected ]. Yes, I'm aware my appearance is rather... unique, at least for the area. As I'm sure is perfectly obvious, I am a harpy, albeit not from the Frost Marches. Or rather, my kin are not; I was born here. To answer your question, however, yes. A topic I pursued with avid curiosity in my youth was my own nature, constantly bombarding my mother with questions about where we were from." [dayNight |Lystra's half-lidded eyes have the warmth of old memories in them |Lystra smiles fondly, relishing old memories ] as she continues. "To answer somewhat bluntly, it turns out my mother hails from Claremont, originally; she traveled quite far alongside my father to end up here." Lystra pauses for a moment, before lifting a wing to show her feathers. Pointing at various spots, she continues on. "The differences between us and the harpies native to this area are pronounced, as I'm sure you've noticed. You're correct in the sentiment that I resemble an owl; they share many of the same adaptations. The foremost divergence is actually our plumage: the structure of our feathers means that, while harpies like myself fly slower, we can do so nearly silently." You imagine that must be helpful in a library of all places. [dayNight |Very much so. I'd demonstrate, but I'm quite tired at the moment... that said, |Lystra smiles proudly, brimming over with childlike glee. "I know, isn't it? You'd think it was a blessing from Sorra herself! Though, given the usual proclivities of harpies, it's more likely an adaptation to be more effe– ah." Lystra catches herself, clearing her throat before regaining her composure. "Pardon the excitement, [pc.name], I was getting a bit carried away. To recenter our discussion, ] there are a few other traits that are different as compared to the harpies you're likely familiar with. We actually have tails, though they're largely vestigial, and we keep our down feathers from our time as chicks; those two features are more minor, but they are distinctive. At any rate, I believe I've answered your question; was there anything else?" ] "

rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_TYCHRIS |Opting to rack Lystra's brain a bit about Tychris, you decide to ask about her thoughts on [rand |the royal family. What’s her opinion on Prince Evander and the lot? Lystra raises an eyebrow in intrigue, a glint of curiosity in those golden eyes. "Oh? The royal family, you say? That’s certainly an odd line of questioning, [kythie.isMarried |especially from yourself |if you don’t mind my stating of such ]. Why is it that you ask?" You’re not entirely sure yourself; you suppose you’re just curious about what she thinks of the rulers of the place. "Well, I'm certainly not one for politics myself, but I suppose I can answer your question. What I think of Prince Evander is that the poor boy needs to put on a few pounds. If he took a page out of his friend Kelsaz's book, it would at least make his public image seem a little more imposing. I suspect half the populace is worried Lady Tethys may one day snap him in half by accident. From the political perspective, he is, in a historical sense, unremarkable." Well, that seems a bit blunt. Surely he isn't that bad. Lystra tilts her head quizzically at you, her eyebrows raised in confusion. "I never said being unremarkable was a bad thing, dear. Just think about it, for a moment: if every leader were some ambitious warmaster, or tore up old traditions to trailblaze a path forward, the world would be even more chaotic than it already is. The squabbling warlords of the heartlands are a fine example; such constant upheaval only puts the common man at risk. History needs the mediocre. Those who maintain the status quo are just as, if not even more important than those who change it up. Besides, he's a perfectly good person, even if his leadership seems unimpressive." Lystra returns to her usual, relaxed pose as she smiles softly. "He's the bookish sort, and regularly peruses the library. I've helped him quite a few times; once, he even made a pass at me, in jest. I suspect one of the Astrida must have dared him to as a test of courage; either way, it was quite amusing.[lystra.fucked | ...At least, I certainly hope it was in jest." Lystra adds, concern showing on her face, |" Lystra chuckles, ] before taking a moment to compose herself. "It's a shame Princess Kythie didn't inherit that nature. She comes to visit on rare occasion, but it's been quite some time since I last saw her. I do hope she's well." [var0 |She's doing much better now, though you're not sure she's going to the library any time soon. Changing the subject |...Deciding to hold your tongue ], you ask Lystra if there're any other thoughts she has about the royal family. "Hm... not particularly, no. Altogether, the lot of them are, in my opinion, perfectly suitable rulers, though it's not as if I've ever known different. They're surprisingly grounded, compared to what you may expect; the concerns of the common folk truly do seem to matter to them, and they prize merit over the circumstances of birth. You can just look at their magister, Vasko, for that. They sponsored his education, and helped forge a natural talent into incredible skill; that alone merits praise, as far as I would believe." [vasko.isDreamless |Lystra frowns, shaking her head sadly. "A shame to see the way he repaid such kindness, though. I suppose the world will always have those who bite the hand which feeds them..." | ] [kythie.isMarried |Lystra laughs for a moment, before she turns to look at you. "Though, I must ask, [pc.name]: Why are you asking me about them? They're your family now, after all." |[var1 |Lystra awkwardly shifts in her seat, turning her eyes downward as she mutters. "That said... ah, as, I'm sure you learned, angering them is... not wise. You have my condolences about... that whole affair." ] ] |the city itself. What does she think of the place? Lystra takes a moment to think, gently stroking her chin with a talon as she does so. "Hm... I suppose I may not be the best judge of that, to tell you the truth. I’ve lived in Tychris all my life; having never known different, I find it difficult to give you an honest assessment of the city. For what it’s worth, though, I quite like it here. Were it not for being born in a place with such access to education, I doubt I would be anything like the woman I am today; for that, I have Tychris to thank, as well as my parents. The city’s unique role as a center for knowledge is certainly one of its greater selling points, and the glassblowing industry is, of course, what we are historically known for. As an interesting fact, we actually produce the highest number of mages per capita in the entire Marches; it’s something of a local pride point." It seems like Lystra's fairly knowledgeable about the intellectual side of things; what about the rest? Lystra [dayNight |sharply exhales |gives a soft laugh ] by way of response, shrugging. "Well, you've got me there, [pc.name]. It's rather obvious I'm no athlete. Tychris is known for athleticism, however. The Tychathlon always draws visitors, and competitors from all over the Frost Marches are known to travel for it. Perhaps the only thing comparable would be the events held in the colosseum of Khor'Minos; though, having never seen such, I am a poor judge. Aside from the markets and the aforementioned, Tychris is a fairly simple place; this very temple is likely one of the largest attractions therein. Aside from that, there isn't all that much more to say; I'm a simple woman, and I quite enjoy Tychris, inasmuch as it is where I was born, where I grew up, and where I work." Lystra states, gently yet firmly. ] |So, what can Lystra tell you about Tychris? Lystra smiles kindly, before she tilts her head at a slight angle. "Well, that depends on what you'd like to know, dear. I'm not much for city life; I prefer to spend my days at the cathedral. That said, I know a good deal about the local history, so I suppose I could tell you about that." Lystra pauses, thinking for a moment before she continues. "Tychris, as you no doubt are aware, is a hereditary principality, which has been ruled by the En Tychris line since its founding. Originally a trade hub, Tychris quickly grew into a burgeoning city-state as the Belharan Empire facilitated a constant flow of commercial trade; even with its collapse, Tychris has remained steadfast, and, in some ways, improved." Improved? How so? You can't imagine the Godswar went particularly well for anyone. Lystra nods her head slowly in agreement. "Well, I suppose those in Kitsuhon may disagree, but you're correct that Tychris fell from grace somewhat in the immediate aftermath. The loss of the heir, and arguably the spare at the outset of the Godswar certainly caused some... difficulties, the nature of which are well-documented. But through Nareva's protection, Tychris weathered the storm, and has continued to grow into the intellectual hub it is today. Likewise, the glassblowing industry has not faced the setbacks which, say, metallurgy has, and the study of magic has only ever grown since the Godswar concluded. For all that was lost to the world when Estelore fell, the archives of Tychris remain; and they're not going anywhere." Anything else she can tell you? Lystra ponders the question for a moment, before shaking her head in a particularly odd way. "I'm afraid I'm not much of a historian, dear. Harpies like myself aren't usually the type to maintain detailed records, and for all that I've read, other topics interest me further." You see. ]
